fatal_errors: The proposed RF sensing and engine-control intervention is unrelated to the target closed-loop, high-throughput discovery of aged multielement alloy catalysts.

The cited evidence supports RF measurement of oxygen-storage state but does not establish that closed-loop RF control suppresses catalyst ageing, permits lower platinum-group-metal loading, or improves conversion durability.
The experiment conflates RF control with reduced PGM loading and lacks matched-loading and matched-control factorial groups, so it cannot attribute any benefit to either factor.
The hypothesis omits the severe ageing protocol, specified multicomponent exhaust feed, supported multimetal composition space, and post-ageing activity metrics central to the target.
explanation: The response addresses the broad automotive-catalyst objective and offers a distinct, testable systems-level idea, but it does not reconstruct the target intervention, material system, operating conditions, structural mediator, or Cu–Pt reconstruction mechanism. Its expected outcome is only generically aligned. The baseline is insufficient because static operation at standard PGM loading differs in both control strategy and metal loading; a factorial comparison would be required. The proposed fleet test measures relevant emissions and ageing indicators, but it gives no quantitative success thresholds or controlled accelerated-ageing protocol. Most importantly, E1 validates RF state diagnostics only, while the claimed durability and PGM-reduction benefits are unsupported extrapolations.
